Eric's size rule (2026-09-15): ~250 lines is not a hard cap. The spike must contain, in this order:

5. Hook-latency argument: the current hook path imports (header, LazyModule, SPD-016's 25 ms compile and 11 ms import figures), the import set of `spud hook PreToolUse` after the split, which modules are imported lazily by which commands, and the timing recipe to run before and after (a concrete command Eric can run; measure the current figure now with hyperfine if installed, else a shell loop, and put the number in the spike).

7. ## Result
Produced docs/spikes/spd-065/spud-ledger.md (1034 lines, all nine sections). Recommends one namespace, many files: bin/spud_ledger.py stays the entry and executes 57 part files under bin/spud_ledger.d/ (core, state, render, imports, commands, projects, hooks, shell, cli) into its own globals in a fixed load order. Every name stays a spud_ledger attribute and every monkeypatch lands; the launcher hands the entry its get_code, so every part's bytecode caches in the home's state directory mirroring its path, and nothing is written without that directory. A hook run loads 34 parts; the rest load for commands or on first attribute access. Verified: the move list covers all 734 top-level names (727 statements) exactly once, by script; no definition-time order violation. Real modules with from-imports rejected on evidence: a 10-part cycle and 27 back-edges. Measured with a timing harness (scratch home, 30 interleaved rounds): PreToolUse(Bash) 22.7 ms today vs 23.1 ms with the lazy prototype (eager 25.1 ms); CLI board 35.1 vs 37.2 ms. A prototype generated mechanically from the move list ran the suite in scratch copies: Ran 702; failures matched control's 4 git-dependent tests plus exactly the 3 test_launcher tests listed as mechanical edits. A 36-step CLI and hook smoke session was identical except random member names. Left: 9 open questions for Eric (the join, lazy vs eager, cache-rule owner, directory name, guard test, probes, merge window, 9 parts over 250 lines kept whole, headless.py copy); CLAUDE.md line 19 and line 170 (says 732, suite runs 702) for Spud. A confirming suite run in the real checkout was started, showed two early failures in test_acceptance (the HEAD ledger round trip; this spike changes no code) and was stopped unfinished; Phase 2 runs the suite there. Proposal 76 filed (tests/probes/headless.py copies only bin/spud, broken since SPD-016). My scratchpad timing and smoke scripts ran spud init only against temporary scratch homes, as the suite does.

Accepted. docs/spikes/spd-065/spud-ledger.md (1034 lines) has all nine sections against bin/spud_ledger.py at 9e1deda (11065 lines, 734 names). It recommends one namespace across 57 part files under bin/spud_ledger.d/, loaded in a fixed order by the entry, with hooks loading only the 34 parts they need. The move list was checked by script. Latency was measured: hooks at parity (22.7 vs 23.1 ms), commands about +2 ms. A mechanically built prototype passed the 702-test suite in scratch copies, with only the four git-dependent tests the control also fails and the three launcher tests listed as mechanical edits. Nine parts sit over ~250 lines, all recommended kept whole. Nine open questions go to Eric for approval before Phase 2.
